IPO. Ride-hailing firm Angkas with passenger is seen navigating the elliptical Road in Quezon City on January 10, 2020.
Hidden among the many displays at the ASEAN Business and Investment Summit (ABIS) was a little clue about where the popular motorcycle taxi company Angkas was headed to next: a location pin pointed right at the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE).
While business leaders were busy rubbing elbows in Solaire’s Grand Ballroom for ABIS , Angkas founder and CEO George Royeca was making moves of his own, meeting in the same hotel with some of the country’s top officials.
Here, Royeca announced the company’s plans to go public. And he had quite the audience.
At the ceremony were First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, and ASEAN Business Advisory Council (ABAC) chair Joey Concepcion, among others.
In a message to Rappler, Royeca confirmed that Angkas was targeting an initial public offering (IPO) by the second half of 2027.
“Yes, H2 of 2027,” Royeca said. “Working with our underwriters.”
Asked about the potential size of the offering, Royeca said it was “still in the works.” What he was more forthcoming about was where the money would go.
“It’s for growth capital, expanding motorycle taxis nationwide, and bringing opportunities to 4.7 million tricycle drivers across the country,” he told Rappler.
And if “Mister Angkas” needed any encouragement, he certainly got some from no less than the First Lady, who had plenty of warm words.
“You used your talent, determination and entrepreneurial spirit to give thousands of motorcycle riders a chance to earn an honest living and provide for their families,” Araneta-Marcos said in a Facebook post.
“From those early conversations to Angkas’ journey toward an IPO — ang layo na talaga ng narating ninyo (you’ve truly gone far)!”
Royeca expressed his appreciation to the First Lady and thanked the Angkas riders who “stood by us through the most difficult times.”
Recto also welcomed the announcement, saying that he hoped Angkas’ planned listing would encourage more Filipino companies to raise capital through the local stock market and give Filipinos more opportunities to invest.
The company is targeting more than 200,000 retail investors for its planned IPO, according to Recto.
Of course, Angkas still has quite the road ahead before ringing the bell at the PSE. For one, it still needs to work out details like its offering size, valuation, and timeline with underwriters and regulators. But after homegrown e-wallet giant Mynt’s succesful IPO in 2026, the local motorcycle taxi pioneer might just be the next app-based company to go public. – Rappler.com
